title: The Technological Singularity
pitch: A short, calm guide from a DeepMind and Imperial College researcher to how we might get to superintelligence and what it would mean.

chapters.g: Two broad routes to human level AI: copy the brain, or engineer intelligence from scratch.
Scanning and simulating a brain in detail, what it would take and what we would get.
Building AI from machine learning and other methods, without copying biology.
How human level AI could become superintelligent, through speed, scale and self-improvement.
Could such systems be conscious, and why it matters for how we treat them.
Effects on work, society, and the balance of power.
The best and worst outcomes, and what we can do to make the good ones more likely.

ideas: There are two main routes to AI: brain emulation and engineered AI.
Engineered AI might be stranger and harder to predict than emulated brains.
Superintelligence could follow human level AI quickly.

args.a: The singularity is a serious possibility worth planning for.
args.c: Skeptics say AI will hit limits long before anything like a singularity.

questions: Would a brain emulation be safer than an engineered AI?
Which chapter changed your mind the most?

quiz.q: What are Shanahan's two routes to AI?
o: Brain emulation and engineering from scratch

quiz.q: What is the last chapter called?
quiz.w: It weighs the best and worst outcomes.
